sentences.text: Hesperosuchus agilis is the sole species within the extinct genus Hesperosuchus, a member of the crocodylomorph reptiles.
This animal belongs to the superorder Crocodylomorpha and is classified within the unranked family Sphenosuchia, placing it in the class Reptilia.
Its body featured large, strong hind limbs and smaller, more slender forelimbs with five fingers on each, supporting a light frame built for rapid movement.
The skull was tall and narrow, resembling theropod dinosaurs rather than modern crocodilians, and held lanceolate-shaped teeth that were serrated on both edges.
Along its back, the animal possessed two paired rows of roughly square osteoderms, each bone overlapping the one behind it with a straight, raised keel on the upper surface.
The dentition and jaw structure suggest Hesperosuchus may have had lips to protect its teeth, a feature not seen in modern crocodilians.
Fossilized stomach contents reveal that this reptile was part of the diet of the primitive predatory theropod dinosaur Coelophysis.
Remains were discovered in Northern Arizona by Llewellyn I. Price, William B. Hayden, and Barnum Brown between 1929 and 1930, and the genus was formally named by Colbert in 1952.
Fossils have been found in Late Triassic rock layers across Arizona and New Mexico.
As a terrestrial animal, speed and the ability to run fast were key survival traits for Hesperosuchus.
During the Triassic, the landscape of Northern Arizona where it lived was surrounded by lakes and streams.
It lived at the same time as Coelophysis, a primitive predatory theropod dinosaur.
Hesperosuchus lived from the Norian to the Rhaetian stages, between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago.
Bones previously thought to be juvenile Coelophysis found in adult stomachs were later identified as belonging to Hesperosuchus or a similar animal.

It is debated whether later specimens found in the same formation belong to H. agilis, as the time gap between them is at least 20 million years and species differentiation is difficult without complete skeletons.
